items.next_action: Require vessel purpose, fluid, port arrangement and pressure data before selecting geometry or safety parts.

items.preferred_term: hydraulic separator or low-loss header only for a low-resistance primary-secondary interface
items.candidate_term: header, manifold, buffer tank or hydraulic separator
items.issue: All can appear as enlarged pipe bodies with several ports. A hydraulic separator decouples circuit flows; an ordinary header distributes branches; a manifold serves repeated circuits; a buffer tank stores significant water volume. Some products combine functions, but the roles are not automatic synonyms.
items.next_action: Store the hydraulic function and each port role; allow combined products only when supported by selected product evidence.

items.preferred_term: thermostatic radiator valve for local radiator modulation and room thermostat for an electrical zone demand
items.issue: A TRV head mechanically operates its own radiator valve in response to local temperature. A room thermostat sends a control request to valves, actuators, pumps or the heat source. They can coexist and have different placement and wiring.
items.next_action: Generate each physical control only when present and prevent furniture or covers from invalidating its intended sensing location.

items.preferred_term: one continuous underfloor-heating loop with paired flow and return manifold ports
items.candidate_term: floor-heating pipe grid, heating coil or floor zone
items.issue: A loop is a continuous pressure circuit, commonly without concealed intermediate joints, that leaves one flow port and returns to its matching return port. A room zone may contain several loops controlled together and is not itself a pipe object.
items.next_action: Keep circuit identity, continuous route, length, spacing and paired manifold ports explicit; treat zone grouping as control data.

items.preferred_term: gypsum plasterboard as the generic Australian object, with Gyprock as a proprietary search term and drywall as regional language
items.candidate_term: Gyprock, plasterboard and drywall as identical canonical product names
items.issue: Gyprock is a CSR trade mark that is widely used colloquially in Australia. Drywall is common North American language and can also refer to the wider construction method. Product brand, generic material and assembly must remain distinguishable.
items.next_action: Let all three terms find the object, retain plasterboard as the Australian generic name and keep the selected manufacturer and product separately.

items.preferred_term: lining for the wall or ceiling covering and separate trim, accessory and service objects attached to it
items.candidate_term: wall lining including skirting, cornice, architrave, switches and power points
items.issue: Attachments touch and visually complete a lined wall but have different materials, quantities, ownership and replacement. Treating every attachment as lining makes junction and take-off data unusable.
items.next_action: Connect trims, accessories and services to the lining with explicit relationships instead of merging their geometry or material identity.

items.preferred_term: selected plasterboard product and documented grade or system role
items.candidate_term: white board, green board, blue board, red board or acoustic board chosen by face colour
items.issue: Manufacturers use different colours and branded ranges. Water, fire, acoustic, impact and multi-performance properties belong to a selected product and complete system, not a universal colour code.
items.next_action: Require a product or explicit performance role; keep colour as appearance metadata only.

items.preferred_term: wall-lining furring channel, external cladding furring channel, acoustic resilient channel and ceiling furring channel as separate roles
items.issue: Similar cold-formed sections can support different faces, loads, clips and performance systems. A section name without host, orientation and role is not enough to select geometry or connections.
items.next_action: Ask for wall or ceiling, internal or external, support method and acoustic role before selecting a channel family.

items.preferred_term: direct-fixed ceiling for sheets or channels attached close to structure and suspended ceiling for a hanger-supported grid below it
items.candidate_term: dropped, battened, direct-fixed and suspended ceiling as interchangeable descriptions
items.issue: The systems have different load paths and parts. A direct-fix clip transfers load straight to nearby structure; a suspended grid requires anchors, hangers, primary and secondary members and restraint design.
items.next_action: Store the structural endpoint and support topology before generating the ceiling grid.

items.preferred_term: exposed-grid suspended ceiling, concealed suspended plasterboard ceiling or another named system
items.issue: Everyday terms describe a ceiling below the primary structure but do not say whether the finish is continuous plasterboard, removable lay-in tile, linear plank, baffle or another system.
items.next_action: Use false or drop ceiling for search, then request the visible finish and support system.

items.preferred_term: Level 3, 4 or 5 plasterboard finish as a specified finish requirement and inspection attribute
items.candidate_term: Level 5 material layer or Level 5 plasterboard object
items.issue: A level of finish describes the required jointing and surface preparation outcome under relevant viewing and decoration conditions. It is not an extra board or universally a single separate coating solid.
items.next_action: Attach the specified level, decoration, lighting and acceptance evidence to the complete lining surface; generate only the actual selected materials.

items.preferred_term: plasterboard back-block bonded behind a joint, sheet-edge backing fixed behind an edge, and framing nogging as separate members
items.candidate_term: back block, backing, blocking and nogging
items.issue: A plasterboard back-block spreads stress behind a joint. Edge backing provides a fixing surface. A nogging is part of wall framing. Their materials, positions and load paths differ.
items.next_action: Use material, face relationship, host and joint role to select the object; never infer it from the word block alone.

items.preferred_term: paper plasterboard tape, glass-mesh tape, fibre-cement tape, fire-system tape and acoustic-system tape as documented products
items.issue: The tapes can differ in material, alkali resistance, compound compatibility and tested-system role. Similar width or mesh appearance does not make them interchangeable.
items.next_action: Bind tape to board, compound and performance system; permit substitution only from explicit selected-system evidence.

items.preferred_term: external corner, internal corner, stopping, casing, shadowline and control-joint bead as separate profiles
items.issue: All are long edge sections, but they form different positive or negative corners, exposed edges, caps, recesses and movement breaks. Profile and function determine geometry.
items.next_action: Select by corner sign, board thickness, exposed face, movement function and adjoining construction.

items.preferred_term: shadowline as a visible recessed edge and control joint as a deliberate movement break
items.candidate_term: shadow gap, control joint and expansion joint
items.issue: A shadowline may be purely visual and rigidly fixed. A control joint separates lining edges to accommodate movement. A building expansion joint can require much greater structural movement and a coordinated system through many layers.
items.next_action: Store movement requirement, separated layers and continuity systems before treating a visible gap as a control joint.

items.preferred_term: recessed-edge joint for factory-recessed sheet sides and butt joint for square-cut sheet ends
items.issue: A recessed joint has room for tape and compound within the board recess. A butt joint builds above flat faces and often needs backing, staggering or broad feathering. Their drawing and quantity logic differs.
items.next_action: Derive joint type from the actual sheet-edge profiles and support relationship rather than line orientation alone.

items.preferred_term: cornice as decorative junction trim, cornice adhesive as its fixing, and any required air, acoustic or fire seal as a separate object
items.issue: Cornice and its bedding can hide a wall-to-ceiling gap. That appearance does not prove continuous air, acoustic, smoke or fire sealing behind it.
items.next_action: Draw the cornice and bedding, then require the selected performance seal behind or beside it when the assembly needs continuity.

items.preferred_term: general internal fibre-cement lining, wet-area substrate, compressed floor sheet and external cladding as separate product roles
items.issue: Cement sheet is broad trade language and Villaboard is proprietary. Density, thickness, edge, exposure, fixing, joint and finish requirements differ between wall, floor, internal, external and wet-area products.
items.next_action: Use cement sheet and brand terms for search, then require product, classification, location, exposure and finish role.

items.preferred_term: service object, lining cut-out, trimmer support and performance seal as separate connected objects
items.candidate_term: hole for light, grille, pipe or outlet
items.issue: The service body is not the opening. A cut lining edge may need framing and trim, the service may need independent support and fire, acoustic, air or moisture continuity may need another tested system.
items.next_action: Create the rough opening and its support first, connect the selected service and add every required continuity system explicitly.

items.preferred_term: interior plywood lining to AS/NZS 2270 scope only for a fully protected non-structural interior role unless other evidence is selected
items.candidate_term: ply lining suitable for bracing, wet areas, exterior use or fire performance
items.issue: Interior plywood can be an appearance panel without being structural plywood, exterior plywood, marine plywood or a tested fire-hazard product. Similar veneer geometry conceals major bond and grade differences.
items.next_action: Store grade, bond, product standard, structural role, exposure and fire evidence independently.

items.preferred_term: stud adhesive, masonry direct-fix bed, back-blocking adhesive, panel adhesive and cornice adhesive as separate installed roles
items.issue: Adhesives differ by substrate, chemistry, load path, application pattern and required mechanical fixing. A cartridge or bag shape is not enough to select the installed object.
items.next_action: Ask for both substrates and physical purpose, then generate the documented bead, daub or bed plus required mechanical fixings.

items.preferred_term: ceiling grid supports lining or tiles and building services use their own support unless the ceiling system is explicitly designed for them
items.candidate_term: light, diffuser, duct, cable tray or pipe supported by the ceiling
items.issue: A service may fit within a grid module while its mass and operating loads bypass the tile and ceiling grid. Visual alignment does not prove structural support or allowed service load.
items.next_action: Persist support ownership and trace each load to verified structure; never derive support from intersection with a grid module.

items.preferred_term: Group Number, sound rating, impact result, moisture suitability, anchor capacity and finish level as evidence linked to physical products and assemblies
items.candidate_term: fire sheet geometry, acoustic wall thickness, compliant anchor shape or Level 5 surface solid
items.issue: These are test, design, product or workmanship results. Geometry can expose the members being assessed but cannot prove the result without the applicable edition, system, project inputs and evidence.
items.next_action: Keep optional analysis overlays out of material take-off and attach every result to its selected product, system, standard edition and project evidence.

items.preferred_term: door leaf for the complete moving closure and panel only for a leaf infill or clearly identified sliding or folding panel role
items.issue: Panel can mean an infill inside a stile-and-rail leaf, a complete sliding panel, a folding panel or an informal name for any door leaf. Mapping it without context can create the wrong hierarchy and geometry.
items.next_action: Ask whether panel means the complete moving element, a joinery infill, a sliding panel or a folding panel before generating geometry.

items.preferred_term: jamb for the fixed frame member and stile for the moving leaf member
items.issue: A frame jamb stays fixed in the wall opening. A door stile moves with a panelled leaf. Both are vertical and may carry hinges or closing hardware, so shape alone does not distinguish them.
items.next_action: Store whether the member is fixed to the opening or moves with the leaf before assigning jamb or stile.

items.preferred_term: hollow-core door leaf with a perimeter frame, face skins, cellular infill and local hardware reinforcement
items.issue: A hollow-core leaf is not an empty shell. It normally contains cellular support, edge framing and a limited lock block. Treating it as empty loses fixing zones and creates unsafe assumptions about cut-outs and hardware.
items.next_action: Persist the selected core, perimeter and hardware-reinforcement zones even when low-detail display hides the interior.

items.preferred_term: solid-core leaf as a construction family, with fire, acoustic and security performance stored as separate selected evidence
items.candidate_term: solid-core means fire door or soundproof door
items.issue: A dense core changes mass and hardware support but does not by itself prove an FRL, fire-door approval, acoustic rating, smoke control or security performance.
items.next_action: Generate the physical core and attach any fire, acoustic or security result only from the selected documented doorset or test evidence.

items.preferred_term: lock block for the limited concealed reinforcement zone inside a lightweight leaf
items.candidate_term: the hollow-core door has solid timber everywhere around the handle
items.issue: Lock blocks can be limited in height, depth and handing. Assuming a full-height or two-sided solid zone can place a latch, pull or hinge outside the manufacturer's supported area.
items.next_action: Require the selected leaf's marked lock side and documented reinforcement extent before cutting or fixing hardware.

items.preferred_term: door stop moulding, open-position door stop, sliding track stop and folding track stop as separate objects
items.issue: Door stop may mean the fixed jamb moulding that locates a closed leaf, a wall or floor buffer that limits swing, or an end stop inside a sliding or folding track. These have different hosts, loads and quantities.
items.next_action: Ask whether the requested stop controls the closed position, swing travel, sliding travel or folding guide travel.

items.preferred_term: flush-finish or architrave-free metal door frame
items.issue: The finished opening can look frameless because perforated frame flanges are jointed into the wall. A physical steel head, jambs, rebate, hinge support and strike preparation are still present.
items.next_action: Treat frameless as an appearance or search term and always draw the selected concealed frame and lining junction.

items.preferred_term: dummy door furniture for a fixed handle or knob with no spindle-operated latch
items.issue: Dummy describes the furniture function, not the door leaf. A dummy handle can still act as a real pull on a cupboard, roller-catch door or inactive leaf.
items.next_action: Keep the leaf normal and set the furniture function to fixed pull with no latch mechanism.

items.preferred_term: surface-sliding internal door
items.issue: Barn door is useful trade language for an exposed face-of-wall track style but does not identify all surface sliders and can imply an aesthetic rather than the support, guide and anti-jump hardware.
items.next_action: Accept barn door for search, then require a surface-mounted track topology and selected hardware system.

items.preferred_term: passage, privacy, dummy and keyed functions stored separately from lever, knob, rose or backplate shape
items.issue: The visible handle shape does not say whether a latch, privacy release, key cylinder, deadbolt or no operating mechanism is present. One furniture design can be sold in several functions.
items.next_action: Ask for function first, then furniture form, finish, backset, leaf thickness and frame strike.

items.preferred_term: split-jamb lining at a cavity pocket mouth and split stud within the pocket frame as separate members
items.candidate_term: cavity slider split jamb or split stud
items.issue: The visible split-jamb trims flank the moving leaf at the opening. The split studs are wall-pocket frame members behind the lining. Confusing them breaks both finish quantities and leaf clearance checks.
items.next_action: Store visible finish-member and structural pocket-member roles separately even when a product catalogue uses shortened wording.

items.preferred_term: project-selected NCC edition and jurisdiction overlay
items.candidate_term: the current Australian NCC applies everywhere on the same date
items.issue: The NCC is adopted through state and territory systems with local commencement, transition and variation. Tasmania's public notice records NCC 2025 commencement on 1 May 2026 while the repository preserves the edition from which existing national facts were extracted.
items.next_action: Require project jurisdiction, relevant approval date, transition status and adopted edition before presenting any door configuration as a compliance result.

items.preferred_term: structural floor, subfloor, underlayment and underlay as separate physical roles
items.issue: A structural floor carries loads, a subfloor provides the base, an underlayment sheet prepares that base, and an underlay cushions or acoustically separates a finish. One product can perform more than one role, but the roles are not interchangeable.
items.next_action: Ask what carries load, what receives the finish and whether the intermediate layer is a rigid preparation sheet or a resilient underlay.

items.preferred_term: floating floor for a joined finish raft that is not bonded through its field
items.issue: Floating boards are joined to one another and move as a field over an underlay. Adhesive-free resilient products may still use perimeter, seam or grid retention. Neither means that unrestrained pieces are simply dropped on the floor.
items.next_action: Store board-to-board jointing, field bond, local retention and perimeter movement as separate installation properties.

items.preferred_term: engineered timber board and laminate plank as different product constructions
items.issue: Engineered timber has a real timber wear layer over a stabilising core. Laminate normally has a transparent resin overlay and printed decor over a fibreboard core. Similar timber appearance does not make their layers or repair methods the same.
items.next_action: Resolve the exposed wear layer and core construction before choosing geometry, sanding behaviour or finish metadata.

items.preferred_term: hybrid rigid-core plank with its actual SPC or WPC core family recorded
items.issue: Hybrid is an Australian market family covering layered rigid click products. Stone-polymer and wood-polymer composite cores have different material make-up, and hybrid does not automatically mean flexible vinyl plank, laminate or waterproof wet-area construction.
items.next_action: Require the selected product's layer schedule, core family, click system and wet-use evidence rather than generating from the word hybrid alone.

items.preferred_term: structural particleboard flooring with verified grade, thickness and edge profile
items.issue: Yellow tongue is widely understood trade language but is associated with proprietary colour coding and does not uniquely specify every structural particleboard flooring product, thickness, exposure condition or installation system.
items.next_action: Accept yellow tongue for search, then require product, thickness, span, grade, edge profile, support layout and exposure instructions.

items.preferred_term: smoothing or levelling compound with documented placement and thickness limits
items.candidate_term: self-levelling makes the floor perfectly level
items.issue: A flowable compound may smooth, flatten or locally level a substrate, but it does not automatically establish a horizontal datum, remove every high spot or suit every timber, concrete, heated or damp substrate.
items.next_action: Store the target tolerance, datum, high-spot removal, primer, compatible substrate and permitted thickness before generating a levelling layer.

items.preferred_term: under-slab vapour barrier, liquid slab moisture barrier, floating-floor vapour retarder and wet-area waterproofing membrane as separate layers
items.issue: The phrase can refer to layers in very different positions with different materials and functions. A liquid treatment under resilient flooring is not an under-slab membrane, and neither automatically replaces a wet-area waterproofing system.
items.next_action: Ask which moisture source is controlled, where the layer sits and whether its role is vapour control, finish protection or wet-area waterproofing.

items.preferred_term: carpet primary and secondary backing as parts of the carpet, with soft underlay as a separate installed layer
items.issue: Backing is manufactured into the textile floor covering and carries or stabilises the pile. Underlay is a separate fibrous, foam, rubber or combination product installed below the carpet.
items.next_action: Keep factory carpet anatomy separate from site-installed underlay and from cushion backing factory attached to a carpet tile.

items.preferred_term: carpet gripper strip with angled pins
items.issue: Smooth edge is common Australian trade language for the timber strip even though the strip contains sharp angled gripper pins. It must not be modelled as a harmless flat trim or confused with a doorway naplock profile.
items.next_action: Accept smooth edge as an alias, but generate the concealed timber strip, angled pins, perimeter offset and separate substrate fixings.

items.preferred_term: carpet seam tape, hot-melt seam adhesive and cut-edge sealer as separate components
items.issue: The hot-melt adhesive bonds the carpet backs to seam tape. Edge sealer binds cut textile edges. They occupy different geometries and one does not replace the other.
items.next_action: Draw backing reinforcement and cut-edge treatment independently and store the selected seaming method.

items.preferred_term: PVC sheet, LVT, flexible vinyl plank, self-adhesive tile and rigid-core hybrid as separate product forms
items.issue: Vinyl may mean roll sheet, flexible tile or plank, a factory-adhesive tile or a rigid click product sold as hybrid. Their seams, joints, adhesives, underlays and movement behaviour differ.
items.next_action: Resolve supplied format, flexibility, core, edge joint and site-fixing method before choosing the drawable assembly.

items.preferred_term: heat-welded resilient finish seam
items.candidate_term: welded vinyl is automatically a waterproof floor
items.issue: A compatible weld rod can close the finish seam, but waterproof performance depends on the whole selected system at substrate, walls, corners, drains, penetrations and terminations. A welded line alone is not compliance evidence.
items.next_action: Treat seam construction and wet-area waterproofing evidence as separate checks tied to the complete selected floor system.

items.preferred_term: timber skirting, scotia or quad, preformed resilient skirting and integral coved sheet upturn as separate perimeter objects
items.issue: The word can mean a board fixed to the wall, a small gap-cover moulding, a separate flexible profile or the floor sheet itself turned up the wall. Each has different geometry, fixing and junctions.
items.next_action: Ask whether the perimeter finish is a board, small moulding, separate resilient extrusion or an integral continuation of the floor sheet.

items.preferred_term: finish transition, doorway threshold and movement-joint cover as different assemblies
items.issue: A transition protects two finish edges, a doorway threshold coordinates door and access geometry, and an expansion-joint cover bridges a moving substrate separation. Similar-looking top caps do not give them the same role.
items.next_action: Resolve adjoining finish levels, doorway constraints and substrate movement before selecting a profile family.

items.preferred_term: dry-area tiled floor and wet-area tiled waterproofing assembly as separate contexts
items.issue: A dry tiled floor can be represented by prepared substrate, adhesive, tile, grout and movement joints. A wet-area floor also depends on falls, waterstops, membranes, drains, penetrations and wall junctions that must not disappear behind the finish label.
items.next_action: Determine the room exposure and applicable wet-area system before assigning the tile to a dry-finish or waterproofed assembly.

items.preferred_term: timber sanding sequence, filler, sealer coat and protective coating as separate operations and materials
items.issue: Polish is common trade language, but many floors receive polyurethane, oil, hardwax oil or another protective system rather than a literal polishing-only process. Sanding also removes material and is limited by board and wear-layer thickness.
items.next_action: Store sanding allowance, grit sequence, filler, sealer and coating chemistry instead of generating one generic polish layer.

items.preferred_term: paint material, application coat, dry film and complete paint system as separate concepts
items.issue: Paint can mean liquid product, one application, the dry film left by that application or the entire preparation-and-coating build-up. Those meanings produce different geometry, quantities and evidence.
items.next_action: Ask whether the input names a product, an application coat, a permanent dry film or the ordered system before generating geometry or quantities.

items.preferred_term: primer, sealer and undercoat as different coating roles
items.issue: Primer mainly establishes substrate adhesion, sealer regulates or isolates the receiving face, and undercoat creates build or uniformity below a finish. Products can combine roles without making the words universal synonyms.
items.next_action: Resolve substrate, coating role and selected product before deciding whether separate first and intermediate coats exist.

items.preferred_term: one combined primer-sealer-undercoat coating where the product supports all three roles
items.issue: A primer-sealer-undercoat can be one physical product and one or more application coats. The three role words do not instruct the tool to draw or quantify three different films.
items.next_action: Store product, role claims and application coat count separately; generate only the physical coats in the documented schedule.

items.preferred_term: decorative exterior paint and waterproofing membrane as separate physical systems
items.issue: An exterior coating can provide colour and surface protection, but a wet-area or other waterproof membrane has classified system geometry, junctions, penetrations and evidence that generic paint does not supply.
items.next_action: Identify the exposure and compliance role; attach exterior paint to the full evidenced wall or wet-area assembly without relabelling it as a membrane.

items.preferred_term: ordinary decorative paint and tested intumescent fire-protective coating as separate systems
items.issue: An intumescent structural coating reacts in fire within a tested substrate, primer, build and topcoat system. Ordinary paint colour, thickness or marketing language cannot create an FRL or fire-protection result.
items.next_action: Route fire-protection requests to the tested fire-safety assembly and preserve its substrate, primer, dry-film build, topcoat and evidence.

items.preferred_term: clear timber coating that leaves grain visible but can change colour and sheen
items.issue: Clear describes transparency, not absence of colour change. Water-borne clear coat, varnish, polyurethane, lacquer and shellac can alter amber tone, contrast and sheen differently.
items.next_action: Store coating family, timber species, approved sample, colour change and sheen rather than translating clear to invisible.

items.preferred_term: timber stain, penetrating oil and varnish as different finish roles
items.issue: Stain primarily colours timber, penetrating oil enters the near surface with low build, and varnish forms a protective film. Some proprietary products combine functions but the physical roles remain distinct.
items.next_action: Record colouring, penetration and film-forming roles from the selected product instead of mapping every translucent timber finish to one material.

items.preferred_term: aggregate-filled texture coating and cement render as separate layers
items.issue: Texture coating is a binder-and-aggregate coating over a prepared substrate, while render is a distinct mineral or polymer-modified levelling and finish layer. Similar rough appearance does not merge them.
items.next_action: Resolve composition, nominal build, substrate-levelling role and product system before choosing coating or render geometry.

items.preferred_term: declared or measured product sheen as a coating attribute
items.issue: Sheen labels are related but their ranges can differ between products and suppliers. They change optical appearance without becoming separate physical boards or universal material classes.
items.next_action: Retain the selected product's declared sheen or test data and use it as rendering metadata rather than converting the label to extra geometry.

items.preferred_term: enamel finish with explicit binder, carrier and sheen
items.issue: Australian architectural enamel can be water-borne acrylic or solvent-borne alkyd and can be supplied in more than one sheen. Enamel alone does not identify chemistry or gloss level.
items.next_action: Ask for the selected product family and sheen before generating trim or door coating data.

items.preferred_term: permanent dry paint film and temporary wet application film as different states
items.issue: Wet-film thickness is measured during application and includes volatile carrier. Dry-film thickness describes the permanent solid material after drying or curing. The values are not interchangeable.
items.next_action: Store wet and dry measurements with their method and stage; draw the completed dry film and retain wet film only as application evidence.

items.preferred_term: lead-paint status supported by a documented survey, sample or suitable test
items.issue: Building age and coating appearance can trigger investigation but do not prove lead content. Automatically labelling old paint creates both safety and data errors.
items.next_action: Record unknown or suspected status until competent investigation identifies the actual hazardous coating field.

items.preferred_term: lead-paint encapsulation, ordinary repainting and removal as different management actions
items.issue: Encapsulation uses a documented management system over suitable retained lead paint and keeps the hazard record. Ordinary repainting is not automatically encapsulation, while removal changes the retained physical field and introduces a different hazardous process.
items.next_action: Require the hazardous-paint management method and evidence, then preserve the retained field and inspection obligations when encapsulation is selected.

items.preferred_term: decorative wallpaper finish and structural or non-structural wall lining as separate objects
items.issue: Wallpaper is a thin decorative finish bonded over a substrate. Plasterboard, fibre cement and other lining sheets form the wall face beneath it. Lining paper is a third, thin preparatory sheet.
items.next_action: Resolve whether the term means the host lining sheet, optional lining paper or exposed decorative wallcovering before drawing the layer stack.

items.preferred_term: paste-the-wall and paste-the-paper as different adhesive-placement topologies
items.issue: Both systems leave adhesive behind the covering, but one applies it to the prepared wall and the other to the sheet backing with possible booking or relaxation. Product construction and handling differ.
items.next_action: Read the selected product's hanging method before placing adhesive or calculating booking and drop workflow.

items.preferred_term: water-activated ready-pasted wallpaper and pressure-sensitive self-adhesive wallcovering as separate systems
items.issue: Ready-pasted backing activates with water, while self-adhesive backing bonds under pressure after a release liner is removed. Their substrate, activation, handling and removal behaviours differ.
items.next_action: Resolve water activation versus pressure-sensitive backing and exclude the temporary release liner from completed-building geometry.

items.preferred_term: wallcovering primer-sealer and wallpaper size as separate preparation roles
items.issue: Primer-sealer creates a compatible sealed receiving face. Size regulates suction, slip and paste behaviour in a selected hanging system. One product can combine roles, but the terms are not universally interchangeable.
items.next_action: Store the product and intended role, then generate separate layers only where the documented wallcovering system physically includes them.

items.preferred_term: finished butt seam and double-cut seam method as related but different concepts
items.issue: Butt seam describes the finished edge-to-edge junction. Double cutting is one installation method that creates matching edges after a temporary overlap. Factory-trimmed drops can also form butt seams without double cutting.
items.next_action: Record the finished junction and the installation method separately; do not retain the temporary overlap as completed geometry.

items.preferred_term: inherent grasscloth fibre, shade and panel variation
items.issue: Natural grasscloth can show visible seams, fibre irregularity and drop-to-drop shading as part of its material character. A seamless digital texture is not the acceptance baseline.
items.next_action: Store the approved sample, batch, top direction and expected natural variation before applying defect checks or texture repetition.

items.preferred_term: ordered multi-panel mural and repeating roll wallpaper as different layout systems
items.issue: A mural reconstructs one composed image from numbered panels and a crop datum. Repeating wallpaper uses roll width, pattern repeat and match rules. Tiling one image cannot serve both systems.
items.next_action: Select image-panel ordering and crop for murals, or roll-repeat and match logic for repeating wallpaper, before generating sheets.

items.preferred_term: cement as a binder constituent and concrete as the hardened composite material
items.candidate_term: cement wall, cement slab or pour cement
items.issue: Cement is a reactive powder within the binder. Concrete combines binder, water and aggregates, with reinforcement or fibres where selected. Treating them as synonyms corrupts material quantities and specifications.
items.next_action: Ask whether the user means supplied cement powder, the full fresh mix or the hardened concrete element before creating material or geometry.

items.preferred_term: concrete, mortar and grout as different cement-based materials
items.issue: These materials can share binder and aggregate ingredients but have different particle sizes, placement roles, structural uses and product evidence. A bearing grout or tendon grout is not ordinary concrete.
items.next_action: Resolve the material's host, aggregate scale and purpose before mapping a generic cement-based mix to an object.

items.preferred_term: cast-in-place and prefabricated concrete as different manufacture and connection topologies
items.issue: The same member role can be cast in its final position or manufactured as a discrete element. Prefabrication adds lifting, transport, bearings, erection bracing and final connections that a cast-in-place solid does not have.
items.next_action: Require manufacture method and element boundaries before generating joints, lifting inserts, bearings or continuous reinforcement.

items.preferred_term: slab-on-ground and suspended slab as separate support conditions
items.issue: A ground slab is supported continuously or through integral beams by prepared ground. A suspended slab spans to discrete walls, beams or columns with space below. Their formwork, load path and reinforcement topology differ.
items.next_action: Resolve the actual support below the slab before selecting ground beams, suspended formwork, span directions or deflection attributes.

items.preferred_term: waffle raft and suspended waffle slab as separate assemblies
items.issue: A waffle raft is ground-supported and commonly formed over pods. A suspended waffle slab spans through intersecting ribs and uses coffers or soffit forms. Similar underside grids do not make their supports or parts interchangeable.
items.next_action: Ask whether the rib grid bears on ground or spans above space, then create pods or suspended coffers accordingly.

items.preferred_term: flat plate without support thickenings and flat slab with drops or capitals
items.issue: Trade and international usage can blur these names. The physical distinction needed by the drawing tool is whether drop panels or column capitals exist at column supports.
items.next_action: Use support-zone geometry as the deciding input and retain the user's wording as an alias if regional documentation differs.

items.preferred_term: structural concrete topping and non-structural screed as different layers
items.issue: A structural topping contributes to composite action or load distribution when designed. A screed generally provides levels, falls or a finish substrate. Thickness and cementitious appearance cannot prove structural participation.
items.next_action: Require the documented structural role and interface connection before classifying a cast layer as structural topping.

items.preferred_term: deep pile and shallow bulk pier as different foundation elements
items.issue: Australian usage can call a shallow enlarged hole a bulk pier and can also call drilled deep foundations piers. Depth, slenderness, installation method and geotechnical load path decide the object, not the word pier alone.
items.next_action: Ask for the geotechnical and installation description before mapping pier to a shallow or deep-foundation family.

items.preferred_term: open-hole bored pile and continuous-flight-auger pile as different installation topologies
items.issue: An ordinary bored pile leaves an excavated shaft before concrete placement. A CFA pile places concrete or grout as the continuous auger is withdrawn and inserts reinforcement into fresh material. Records and temporary states differ.
items.next_action: Store the actual installation method and reinforcement sequence rather than selecting from a cylindrical final shape.

items.preferred_term: reinforcement product form and reinforcement role as separate properties
items.candidate_term: main bar, top bar, distribution bar or N bar
items.issue: Deformed or plain describes the steel product and surface. Longitudinal, transverse, top, bottom, main and distribution describe location or design role. One physical bar can carry several role labels without becoming several solids.
items.next_action: Create one bar geometry and attach product designation, face or layer and all documented design roles as separate attributes.

items.preferred_term: starter bar and joint dowel as different connection roles
items.issue: A starter develops into a later concrete pour to continue reinforcement. A joint dowel can transfer shear and may need one sleeved or debonded end to permit movement. Modelling every projecting bar as fully bonded can lock a movement joint.
items.next_action: Record the joint role, bond state at each end and movement direction before generating bar embedment.

items.preferred_term: lap splice and mechanical bar splice as different force-transfer assemblies
items.issue: A lap uses overlapping bars and surrounding concrete bond. A mechanical splice uses a qualified coupler or grouted sleeve. Their congestion, bar preparation and inspection evidence differ.
items.next_action: Select the documented splice system and preserve its product, bar-end preparation, grout and inspection states.

items.preferred_term: bar chair, cover spacer and cover dimension as separate concepts
items.issue: A chair normally supports a reinforcement layer vertically. A spacer maintains side or soffit cover. Cover itself is the measured concrete distance, not a component. Products can combine roles but the concepts remain distinct.
items.next_action: Store the physical support product separately from the required cover and the direction of load or restraint.

items.preferred_term: construction, contraction, isolation and expansion joints as different designed interfaces
items.issue: A construction joint stages pours, a contraction joint localises shortening cracks, an isolation joint separates a local restraint, and an expansion joint separates moving structural units. Calling all of them expansion joints loses the intended movement and transfer topology.
items.next_action: Require the joint's design intent, reinforcement continuity, dowels, filler and movement before choosing its type.

items.preferred_term: designed concrete joint and accidental crack as different entities
items.issue: A joint has an intended route and components. A crack is a material discontinuity or condition that may be expected, accidental or evidence of distress. A saw-cut contraction joint may guide a crack but the groove and crack are not synonyms.
items.next_action: Keep cracks in condition and inspection data unless a separate defect ontology is added; never auto-upgrade them to designed joints.

items.preferred_term: structural concrete joint waterstop and wet-area waterstop angle as different objects
items.issue: A structural waterstop is embedded in or applied across a concrete joint. A wet-area waterstop angle terminates a membrane at a shower or doorway. Their profiles, hosts and water paths are unrelated.
items.next_action: Resolve the host as a structural concrete joint or a finished wet-area boundary before creating the waterstop profile.

items.preferred_term: cast-in fastening and post-installed fastening as different installation states
items.issue: A cast-in anchor is positioned before concrete placement. A post-installed anchor is drilled or bonded into hardened concrete. Their clash checks, edge evidence and installation inspection differ even when they support the same bracket.
items.next_action: Require installation timing and selected product before choosing cast-in setout or post-installed drilling geometry.

items.preferred_term: blockout, recess and cast-in sleeve as different negative-space topologies
items.candidate_term: leave a hole in the concrete
items.issue: A blockout is a reserved volume, often for later work. A recess is a shallow pocket from one face. A sleeve is a retained tube lining a passage. Their lifecycle, sealing and quantity geometry differ.
items.next_action: Ask whether the passage is full-depth, shallow, lined, temporary or later infilled before generating subtractive geometry.

items.preferred_term: prestressed as the parent family, with pre-tensioned and post-tensioned as different methods
items.issue: Prestressed concrete is the broad family. Pre-tensioned strand transfers force to concrete after casting through bond. Post-tensioned tendons are stressed against hardened concrete through anchorages. Precast does not automatically mean pre-tensioned.
items.next_action: Require the force-introduction method, anchor or transfer zones and casting location before creating tendon components.

items.preferred_term: bonded multistrand tendon and unbonded monostrand tendon as different permanent assemblies
items.issue: A bonded tendon contains strands in a common duct later filled with grout. An unbonded monostrand has grease and a continuous plastic sheath and no grouted common duct. Generating the wrong enclosure changes inspection and no-cut geometry.
items.next_action: Select bonded or unbonded system first, then generate only its applicable duct, sheath, grout, grease and anchorage components.

items.preferred_term: prestressing strand as material component and tendon as the complete force path
items.issue: Strand is the high-strength steel product. A tendon contains one or more strands plus sheath or duct, anchorages and protection. Cable is common speech but can collide with electrical and wire-rope objects.
items.next_action: Model strand paths as children of a tendon assembly and keep cable as a search alias only after context resolution.

items.preferred_term: live-end and dead-end post-tensioning anchorages as different stressing roles
items.issue: The live end is accessible to the stressing jack. The dead end is fixed and not the active jacking end. Both transfer tendon force, but only one needs the same stressing access and recess state.
items.next_action: Record stressing direction and accessible end before creating anchorage recess and jack-clearance geometry.

items.preferred_term: precast as the broad family and tilt-up as a particular casting and erection method
items.issue: All tilt-up panels are prefabricated elements, but many precast panels are cast in factories or beds and lifted without tilting from a slab-on-ground casting position. The manufacture and lifting states differ.
items.next_action: Store factory, casting-bed or site tilt-up manufacture and actual rotation path as attributes rather than treating tilt-up as every precast wall.

items.preferred_term: cast-in lifting anchor, removable lifting clutch and final structural connection as different objects
items.issue: The anchor remains embedded, the clutch is removable lifting equipment, and the final connection transfers in-service actions. One lifting point must not be reused as a structural connection without explicit design.
items.next_action: Attach lifecycle and load-stage roles to every insert and exclude lifting clutches from completed-building geometry.

items.preferred_term: temporary precast panel bracing and permanent structural bracing as different systems
items.issue: Erection braces stabilise panels only until final connections and diaphragms are complete. Permanent braces remain in service. Removing either at the wrong model state changes the load path.
items.next_action: Require erection and release stages, brace design and completed stability evidence before hiding or removing temporary braces.

items.preferred_term: formwork as the mould and falsework as its supporting temporary structure
items.issue: Form faces shape and contain concrete. Falsework carries the formwork and construction loads to foundations. One system can include both, but their members and failure paths differ.
items.next_action: Build a load-path tree from concrete face through sheathing, joists, bearers, props and foundations instead of one generic formwork object.

items.preferred_term: temporary formwork and documented permanent formwork as different lifecycle objects
items.issue: Ordinary formwork is removed. Permanent formwork remains as a deck, lining or protective layer. Remaining in place does not automatically give it composite, structural, fire or finish performance.
items.next_action: Require retained status and each final performance role before including formwork in the completed model.

items.preferred_term: form face, form liner and resulting off-form concrete surface as different objects or states
items.issue: The form face and optional liner are temporary materials. Their inverse texture and joint layout appear on the permanent concrete surface. A formed surface class is evidence and acceptance data, not a coating.
items.next_action: Generate temporary form geometry for construction views and transfer only the documented inverse relief, joints and surface attributes to the completed concrete.

items.preferred_term: manufactured special-purpose unit and documented site-cut unit as different supply states
items.issue: A manufacturer can supply a controlled corner, sill, jamb or closure profile. A site cut changes faces, shells, cores and product evidence. Similar final outlines do not make the supply and quality states identical.
items.next_action: Ask whether the unit is manufactured or cut and retain its actual remaining shell, core and exposed-face geometry.

items.preferred_term: face brick and common brick as exposure roles rather than universal material grades
items.issue: Face brick is selected to remain exposed. Common brick is normally concealed or finished. Neither term by itself establishes material, form, strength, durability or quality.
items.next_action: Store exposure role separately from unit material, form and product classification.

items.preferred_term: masonry closure unit and wall-cavity closer as different objects
items.issue: A closure unit completes masonry bond or wall-end geometry. A cavity closer closes an edge of the wall cavity and may carry moisture, thermal or fire functions.
items.next_action: Require the host: course, cavity edge or opening interface.

items.preferred_term: bond-beam unit and completed reinforced masonry bond beam as different levels
items.issue: The channelled unit is permanent form. The completed structural member also contains reinforcement and grout and needs support, continuity and design evidence.
items.next_action: Generate the unit course, bar route and grout region as related parts rather than one solid block.

items.preferred_term: cleanout unit, temporary cleanout opening and closed completed state
items.issue: The block is a product with a removable or open face. The opening is temporary negative geometry used for cleaning and inspection, then it is closed before grouting.
items.next_action: Retain open, inspected, closed and grouted lifecycle states.

items.preferred_term: masonry screen block for a deliberately open unit
items.issue: Breeze block is useful Australian search language for decorative open screen units. It is not every hollow concrete block and its visible openings remain actual voids.
items.next_action: Ask for the selected screen profile, supports and open-area geometry.

items.preferred_term: running-bond and stack-bond panels as different unit arrangements
items.issue: Running bond offsets vertical joints. Stack bond aligns them and can require different reinforcement and restraint. A surface hatch cannot carry this construction distinction.
items.next_action: Generate actual units and joints from the selected bond and opening setout.

items.preferred_term: header, soldier and brick-on-edge courses as different orientations
items.issue: The three arrangements expose different faces and create different depth, bearing and weathering geometry. None automatically supplies an opening lintel.
items.next_action: Store brick local axes and any concealed support separately.

items.preferred_term: masonry core-fill material and completed grouted core as different objects
items.issue: Core fill or grout is the placed material. The grouted core also includes its connected unit void, reinforcement and inspected placement extent.
items.next_action: Keep the material batch, spatial core route, reinforcement and inspection evidence linked but separate.

items.preferred_term: fully grouted and partially grouted masonry walls
items.issue: Fully grouted work fills all intended connected cores. Partially grouted work fills only scheduled cells and bond beams. The empty-core map is therefore essential geometry.
items.next_action: Require a grouted-cell map and never fill all displayed cores from a generic reinforced-wall command.

items.preferred_term: bed-joint tying mesh and structural masonry reinforcement as different roles
items.issue: AS 2699.2 covers accessory mesh but excludes structural reinforcement in reinforced-masonry bed joints. Similar ladder or mesh shapes can carry different evidence and design roles.
items.next_action: Require accessory or structural role before scheduling mesh.

items.preferred_term: wall tie and general built-in masonry connector as different families
items.issue: Wall ties restrain leaves or veneer in defined wall arrangements. AS 2699.2 connectors also include anchors, wall junction connectors, tie-downs and other accessories.
items.next_action: Ask which hosts are connected and which directions are restrained.

items.preferred_term: masonry shelf angle and opening lintel as different supports
items.issue: A lintel spans a local opening. A shelf angle supports a wall-leaf panel along a floor or frame line and transfers its self-weight through brackets and anchors.
items.next_action: Require support extent, structural host and opening relationship before selecting the member.

items.preferred_term: cavity closer and tested cavity fire barrier as different performance assemblies
items.issue: A closer can finish an edge and contribute thermal or moisture control. A fire barrier needs tested or assessed materials, fixings, continuity and interface evidence.
items.next_action: Never infer a fire role from a cavity being visually filled.

items.preferred_term: autoclaved aerated concrete as the generic material and Hebel as a proprietary search term
items.issue: Hebel is an Australian product brand. AAC is the material family, which can be supplied by different manufacturers and as blocks or reinforced panels.
items.next_action: Preserve AAC as canonical and attach manufacturer, product and system evidence to instances.

items.preferred_term: AAC block masonry and factory-reinforced AAC panel construction
items.issue: Blocks are laid in courses with thin joints. Reinforced panels have factory reinforcement, span orientation, supports and panel fixings. Their cutting and opening rules differ.
items.next_action: Ask block or reinforced panel before generating courses, joints or reinforcement.

items.preferred_term: AAC thin-bed adhesive and ordinary masonry mortar as different joint materials
items.issue: AAC adhesive forms a controlled thin joint in a selected system. Ordinary brick or block mortar has different thickness, workability and unit interaction.
items.next_action: Keep product, joint thickness and compatible AAC substrate explicit.

items.preferred_term: internal AAC panel reinforcement and external render mesh
items.issue: The panel cage is factory-embedded protected steel carrying structural and handling actions. Render mesh is a surface layer controlling the finish system.
items.next_action: Display each mesh at its true depth and never treat render mesh as panel reinforcement.

items.preferred_term: tied stone veneer, adhered stone veneer and anchored stone facade
items.issue: Tied veneer stands on support and uses wall ties, adhered veneer transfers load through a bonded bed, and an anchored facade uses mechanical supports and restraints. The load paths are not interchangeable.
items.next_action: Require construction method, stone thickness, vertical support and face restraint.

items.preferred_term: natural and manufactured stone masonry units
items.issue: Natural stone retains geological source, bedding and quarry variation. Manufactured stone is a factory composite with its own product and installation evidence.
items.next_action: Ask material origin before assigning stone properties or cutting behaviour.

items.preferred_term: ashlar and rubble masonry as different stone layouts
items.issue: Ashlar uses accurately dressed units and regular courses. Rubble uses irregular units, packing and different bond logic. A photo texture cannot replace their unit geometry.
items.next_action: Choose the layout and generate real stone units only to the required level of detail.

items.preferred_term: stone lintel and compression stone arch
items.issue: A lintel bends or spans as a member. An arch transfers compression through voussoirs to springings and abutments. An arched facing can still conceal a separate lintel.
items.next_action: Require structural mechanism and concealed support before treating an arched profile as an arch.

items.preferred_term: stone self-weight support and face restraint as separate anchor roles
items.issue: Support brackets carry gravity reactions. Restraint anchors principally resist face actions and can allow selected movement. One proprietary device may combine roles but both must be recorded.
items.next_action: Store gravity support, face restraint and permitted movement independently for every panel.

items.preferred_term: stone bedding mortar and exposed pointing mortar
items.issue: Bedding mortar supports and bonds the stone through the joint. Pointing mortar forms the exposed outer joint and can be renewed. They can share a mix but are different positions and roles.
items.next_action: Model joint depth zones separately where repair, take-off or heritage compatibility matters.

items.preferred_term: tested building-earth mixture rather than unqualified site soil
items.issue: Earth construction uses a selected particle and moisture blend, sometimes with fibre or stabiliser. Natural site soil may need processing, blending and performance evidence.
items.next_action: Require source, composition, preparation, test evidence and intended construction method.

items.preferred_term: mud-brick masonry and monolithic rammed earth
items.issue: Mud bricks are dried units laid in courses and mortar. Rammed earth is compacted in successive lifts between forms. Their joints, temporary works and repair logic differ.
items.next_action: Ask unit masonry or monolithic compacted earth before generating geometry.

items.preferred_term: compressed earth block and moulded air-dried mud brick
items.issue: Compressed earth block is mechanically pressed. Mud brick is placed wet into a mould and air-dried. Either can include fibre or stabiliser, so manufacture and material composition remain separate axes.
items.next_action: Store forming method, stabiliser and curing separately.

items.preferred_term: stabilised and unstabilised earth as evidence-backed material states
items.issue: Cement, lime or another stabiliser changes composition, embodied impacts and behaviour. It cannot be inferred from colour or assumed for every modern earth wall.
items.next_action: Require stabiliser type and proportion and keep an explicit unknown state when evidence is absent.

items.preferred_term: rammed-earth compacted lift rather than masonry course
items.issue: A lift is one placement and compaction layer in a monolithic wall. It has no separate unit or mortar bed and may not be a construction joint.
items.next_action: Use lift sequence and form-bay extent, not brick-course logic.

items.preferred_term: thin earth slurry finish and thicker earth render
items.issue: A slurry is a thin brushed surface treatment. Earth render is a substantial trowelled or floated coat, commonly containing graded sand and fibre.
items.next_action: Ask for thickness, application method and coat build-up before take-off.

items.preferred_term: solid render layer and later decorative coating system
items.issue: Render is a plaster layer that builds and levels the wall surface. A texture coating is a thinner decorative coating system. Some products blur marketing names but the physical layers remain identifiable.
items.next_action: Store plaster thickness and coating dry film as separate layers.

items.preferred_term: render bond, base, float and finish layers by physical role
items.issue: A splatter bond coat keys the substrate, a base coat builds thickness, a float coat establishes plane and a finish coat provides the outer render surface. A project can combine roles but the evidence must say so.
items.next_action: Generate the selected coat sequence rather than a universal one-layer render.

items.preferred_term: embedded render reinforcing mesh and mechanically fixed render lath
items.issue: Reinforcing mesh is normally embedded in a coat. Expanded-metal lath is fixed to supports and carries render where direct bond is unsuitable. Their fixings, laps and corrosion risks differ.
items.next_action: Ask mesh or lath and require support and fixing data for lath.

items.preferred_term: corner, casing, movement, drip and screed beads by edge role
items.issue: These profiles form different geometry: an external arris, a termination, a moving separation, a water drip or a ruling datum. Substituting one because the section looks similar can bridge joints or lose drainage.
items.next_action: Select bead role first, then material, profile, render depth and exposure compatibility.

items.preferred_term: HB 161:2005 as withdrawn historical plastering guidance
items.issue: HB 161 was a handbook rather than a Standard and was withdrawn in 2018. The current CPCCSP3001 training unit still names it, which explains persistent industry references but does not restore current status.
items.next_action: Label HB 161 historical and require current law, specification and selected-system evidence for project decisions.

items.preferred_term: doorset, door leaf and structural opening as different physical levels
items.issue: A doorset includes leaf, frame, threshold, hardware, seals and fixings. The leaf is only the moving panel, and the structural opening is the wall void and supports receiving the doorset.
items.next_action: Ask which level is intended and keep leaf, product frame and wall opening as separate nested objects.

items.preferred_term: external glazed-door family and solid or composite external-door family
items.issue: A glazed external door may belong to the AS 2047 window-and-external-glazed-door route, while solid timber and composite entrance leaves have different product evidence and construction anatomy.
items.next_action: Choose the physical door family before applying product standards or generating leaf construction.

items.preferred_term: solid core and solid timber as separate descriptions
items.issue: Solid core describes a substantially filled internal construction; it does not mean the whole leaf is one solid timber slab. Particle, stave, mineral or other cores can sit between skins and lippings.
items.next_action: Store core construction and face material separately.

items.preferred_term: joinery panelled leaf and moulded panel-look leaf
items.issue: A traditional panelled leaf has stiles, rails, muntins and separate infill panels. A moulded composite skin can reproduce the same appearance without that joinery anatomy.
items.next_action: Ask whether panel is construction or appearance before generating rails and muntins.

items.preferred_term: door threshold, frame sill and building step by physical role
items.issue: The threshold is crossed by people and seals the leaf bottom; a sill is a lower frame member; a step changes floor level. Products can combine these roles but they are not automatically the same object.
items.next_action: Model crossed profile, frame member and level change independently, then record any combined product.

items.preferred_term: security screen, barrier screen and insect screen
items.issue: An insect screen excludes insects. A barrier screen is a robust secondary closure. A security screen carries classification and test claims for a complete product and installation.
items.next_action: Require a claimed class and traceable evidence before labelling a screen as security.

items.preferred_term: security mesh material inside a classified installed system
items.issue: Stainless mesh, perforated sheet, expanded metal and grilles are infill materials. Security performance also depends on retention, frame, locks, hinges or rollers, receivers, fixings and substrate.
items.next_action: Never promote an infill object to a security claim from material or appearance alone.

items.preferred_term: security, bushfire and fall-prevention screen functions as separate evidence
items.issue: A screen can address forced entry, ember exposure or falls, but each function has different tests, installation details and regulatory context. One claim does not establish the others.
items.next_action: Store each performance role and its source separately on the selected installed system.

items.preferred_term: woven mesh, expanded mesh, perforated sheet and grille by manufacture
items.issue: Woven wire crosses strands, expanded metal is slit and stretched, perforated sheet is punched, and a grille is an open grid of bars or cast members. Their geometry and edge retention differ.
items.next_action: Select infill manufacture and retention before selecting a drawing pattern.

items.preferred_term: external shutter, internal blind and garage door
items.issue: A shutter closes or screens a window or pedestrian opening, a blind is normally a lighter covering, and a garage door closes a large vehicle opening. Similar rolling motion does not make them interchangeable.
items.next_action: Ask opening purpose and scale before choosing shutter or large-access-door anatomy.

items.preferred_term: roller shutter and roller garage door
items.issue: A residential roller shutter commonly uses interlocking slats, compact guides and a boxed roll. A roller garage door commonly uses a continuous corrugated curtain, large guides, drum brackets and a garage-door counterbalance.
items.next_action: Keep the two generators, component libraries and standards routes separate.

items.preferred_term: sectional, roller and tilt garage-door systems
items.issue: A sectional door articulates rigid panels into overhead tracks; a roller door coils a flexible curtain; a tilt door moves one rigid panel through an outward-and-upward path.
items.next_action: Select door kinematics first because every downstream component and clearance depends on them.

items.preferred_term: sectional section and one-piece tilt panel
items.issue: A sectional panel is one of several hinged horizontal sections. A tilt panel is the whole rigid moving closure and follows a different mechanism and swept envelope.
items.next_action: Ask whether panel means a repeated section or the complete one-piece leaf.

items.preferred_term: jamb-fitting and track-fitting tilt mechanisms
items.issue: Jamb fittings guide the panel mainly with side pivot arms. Track fittings use rollers or pivots travelling in overhead tracks. Their supports, travel and clearances differ.
items.next_action: Require the fitting family before generating pivots, tracks or panel sweep.

items.preferred_term: sectional track, roller-door guide and operator drive rail
items.issue: Sectional tracks carry panel rollers, roller-door guides restrain curtain edges, and an operator rail carries a powered trolley. They occupy nearby space but have different loads and attachments.
items.next_action: Name each rail by the moving object it guides.

items.preferred_term: counterbalance and powered operator as separate systems
items.issue: Springs, cables, drums or weights offset door mass. The operator supplies controlled movement to a correctly balanced door; it does not replace the counterbalance or structural supports.
items.next_action: Model and schedule counterbalance before adding an optional operator.

items.preferred_term: torsion spring, extension spring and tilt-door spring
items.issue: A torsion spring twists around a shaft, an extension spring changes length along a cable path, and a tilt fitting uses its selected side-spring geometry. Their anchors and hazards are different.
items.next_action: Identify the spring mechanism without generating setup or adjustment instructions.

items.preferred_term: door lift cable and operator chain or belt
items.issue: Lift cables carry counterbalance force between the door and drums or pulleys. A chain or belt transmits motor output along the operator rail. Neither is an electrical cable.
items.next_action: Store force path, route and moving endpoints for each flexible member.

items.preferred_term: photoelectric beam and sensing safety edge
items.issue: A beam monitors an optical line across the opening before contact. A sensing edge travels on the door and detects contact or deformation. Controller response and monitoring remain separate evidence.
items.next_action: Draw the sensing field and moving edge separately and link each to commissioned control behaviour.

items.preferred_term: inside manual release and outside emergency release
items.issue: The normal manual release is reached from inside and disconnects the trolley or drive. An external keyed release adds a secure penetration and cable path where no other entry exists.
items.next_action: Ask access side and model the external penetration only when selected.

items.preferred_term: roller-door wind lock and centre lock
items.issue: Wind locks are repeated edge fittings engaging reinforced guides under wind. The centre lock is user-operated hardware sending bars into guide receivers to secure the closed door.
items.next_action: Store wind retention and access locking as independent systems.

items.preferred_term: performance rating as evidence-backed metadata on a complete system
items.issue: Wind, security, bushfire, fire, thermal and impact ratings are not visible geometry classes. They depend on a documented product configuration, supports, fixings, size and installation.
items.next_action: Attach rating, scope, source and configuration hash without creating a visual rating subtype.

items.preferred_term: AS 5039.1, AS 5039.2 and AS 5039.3 current security-screen family
items.issue: The reorganised current family separates classification and performance, installation, and test methods. It supersedes the older AS 5039:2008, AS 5040 and AS 5041 pathways.
items.next_action: Store the exact part, edition and amendment used by the selected product and installer.

items.preferred_term: AS/NZS 60335.2.95 edition as project and product metadata
items.issue: The 2024 edition is current, while the 2020 edition remains current during a scheduled transition to 29 November 2027 subject to regulator adoption. A model cannot choose solely from publication date.
items.next_action: Record the edition declared by the product evidence and accepted for the project jurisdiction.

items.preferred_term: headroom, sideroom and backroom as three clearance directions
items.issue: Headroom is space above the opening, sideroom is beside it, and backroom extends into the garage. Door type, track, roll, springs and operator consume different combinations.
items.next_action: Store all three measured directions and the product-specific occupied envelopes.

items.preferred_term: moving, stored and service envelopes
items.issue: The moving envelope follows the door through travel, the stored envelope is occupied when open, and the service envelope preserves access to covers, springs, drives and replaceable parts.
items.next_action: Generate separate non-solid clearance objects for clash checking.

items.preferred_term: counterbalance service state as explicit hazardous lifecycle metadata
items.issue: A spring can be supplied loose, installed without energy, tensioned in service, isolated or damaged. Identical geometry can represent radically different hazards.
items.next_action: Require an explicit unknown or verified service state and never generate adjustment guidance.

items.preferred_term: bottom weather seal, floor threshold and drainage system
items.issue: The moving bottom seal closes a small contact gap, a threshold strip provides a compression land, and site falls or drains manage surface water. None automatically replaces the others.
items.next_action: Keep sealing and drainage roles separate and do not infer flood protection.

items.preferred_term: screen-door pneumatic closer and external-door hydraulic closer
items.issue: A lightweight pneumatic cylinder commonly closes a screen leaf. A controlled pedestrian doorset may use a hydraulic overhead or concealed closer with different forces, brackets and evidence.
items.next_action: Choose closer family from leaf and doorset requirements before drawing brackets.

items.preferred_term: screen track, sliding-door track and garage-door track
items.issue: A screen track guides a lightweight mesh leaf, a sliding glazed door track carries its product panel, and a garage track guides heavy moving sections. Similar channel shapes do not establish interchangeability.
items.next_action: Name tracks by product family and moving object.

items.preferred_term: louvre blade and roller-shutter slat
items.issue: A louvre blade spans a framed panel and is fixed or pivots to control view and air. A roller-shutter slat interlocks with neighbours and must articulate around an axle.
items.next_action: Ask whether the repeated member pivots in a frame or interlocks into a rolling curtain.

items.preferred_term: shutter latch for closed position and holdback for open position
items.issue: A latch transfers actions at the closed or meeting edge. A holdback secures the open leaf against the facade. Their receivers, access and wind actions differ.
items.next_action: Store the retained leaf state and receiver substrate for each fitting.

items.preferred_term: three-point screen lock as one linked system
items.issue: A central screen lock commonly drives remote upper and lower bolts, creating three locking points from one control. It is not necessarily three independent user-operated locks.
items.next_action: Generate one lock body, linkage and documented remote points.

items.preferred_term: operator travel limit and physical track stop
items.issue: An operator limit is sensed or counted control data that stops the motor. A physical track or curtain stop prevents mechanical overtravel. They are complementary, not interchangeable.
items.next_action: Store electronic limit state and physical stop geometry separately.

items.preferred_term: wind-rated door as a complete size-and-installation configuration
items.issue: Door panel or curtain strength is only one part of the wind path. Tracks or guides, wind locks, brackets, supports and fixing schedule must match the documented opening size and rating.
items.next_action: Bind wind evidence to the complete configuration and verified supporting structure.

items.preferred_term: AS/NZS 4505 call-up checked against the adopted NCC clause and project conditions
items.issue: Housing Provisions clause 2.2.4 calls up AS/NZS 4505 for qualifying garage and large access doors in specified wind regions and opening conditions. Online text and adopted editions must be checked for the project jurisdiction.
items.next_action: Store NCC edition, jurisdiction, wind region, opening area and the resulting applicability decision.

items.preferred_term: deck as complete platform and decking as surface material
items.issue: Decking can mean the repeated boards or panels, while deck can mean the whole structure including supports, bearers, joists, connections and edges. Treating them as one object would omit the load path.
items.next_action: Resolve whether a user means the complete platform, its surface assembly or one board before generating geometry.

items.preferred_term: deck, balcony, terrace and verandah as context-dependent platform terms
items.issue: These everyday terms overlap, but support, attachment, roof relation, enclosure and whether occupied space lies below affect the required objects and compliance path.
items.next_action: Store platform topology and the space below rather than choosing a system from the everyday label alone.

items.preferred_term: building-attached and freestanding deck
items.issue: A deck beside a house may be structurally attached through ledgers or brackets, independently supported with a separation joint, or partly tied for lateral stability. Visual proximity does not establish the load path.
items.next_action: Require attachment, bearing and lateral-restraint data before drawing the building interface.

items.preferred_term: open-jointed deck and waterproof platform
items.issue: An open-jointed deck intentionally lets water pass between boards. A waterproof platform uses a continuous external membrane and controlled drainage. Coatings or under-deck trays do not automatically convert the first into the second.
items.next_action: Make surface permeability and the primary water-control plane mandatory system inputs.

items.preferred_term: bearer as supported primary deck member and joist as repeated spanning secondary member
items.issue: Beam may describe several structural roles. In common domestic deck framing, bearers receive repeated joists and span between posts or supports; selecting by the word beam alone can reverse the grid and load path.
items.next_action: Store span direction, support points and supported member family for every horizontal deck member.

items.preferred_term: rim joist as structural edge member and fascia board as edge finish
items.issue: A rim or boundary joist closes, restrains or supports the framing edge. A fascia board covers that edge. One physical board should not be assumed to perform both roles without connection and load evidence.
items.next_action: Keep structural edge and visible finish as separate roles and allow a documented combined instance.

items.preferred_term: deck blocking or nogging identified by restraint role
items.issue: Nogging, noggin and blocking can all describe short pieces between joists, but the required geometry depends on whether they prevent roll, support a joint, transfer a concentrated load or brace a post.
items.next_action: Store the supported joint or restraint function instead of generating generic midspan blocks from the word noggin.

items.preferred_term: deck support post and barrier post
items.issue: A support post carries the platform to a footing. A barrier post resists edge loads and attaches to the edge structure. They can align physically but have different loads, connections and waterproofing consequences.
items.next_action: Require the post role and both end connections before generating or counting it.

items.preferred_term: timber natural durability and preservative treatment as separate properties
items.issue: Natural durability comes from species and relevant wood zone; treatment adds protection to a documented penetration and hazard class. One does not prove the other and neither is inferred from colour.
items.next_action: Store species, heartwood or sapwood zone, natural-durability evidence, treatment standard, hazard class and penetration separately.

items.preferred_term: treatment hazard class as exposure selection metadata
items.issue: A hazard class describes an exposure and treatment target, not a timber species, member size, strength grade, surface finish or proof that every cut end remains protected.
items.next_action: Keep treatment class, structural grade, member role and cut-end treatment as independent attributes.

items.preferred_term: heartwood and sapwood zones
items.candidate_term: one durability value for a timber species
